name: term-sanitize
algorithm: Generate n items of terminal text (splitmix64: printable ASCII, line feeds, e-acute, escapes, C0 controls, C1 controls as C2 80..9F, the euro sign), then rounds times write it with every C0 control but line feed and tab, DEL and every C1 control replaced by U+FFFD, copying each safe run whole, into a buffer; the checksum adds per round the output length and one output byte at a moving index (README.md).

skip.mk-wrap: the checksum already uses the wrapping operators; the loop's other arithmetic is indices bounded by the input

no_counts: B24: the output length counts every replacement (each adds two bytes net for a C0 control or DEL and one for a C1 pair), and the sampled byte changes with what was copied, so a sanitizer that keeps or replaces a different set changes the checksum
notes: Every column generates the text and writes the output with indexed stores into two fixed buffers allocated once and zeroed (calloc, vec![0u8; n], page_allocator then @memset, make, Arena.Slice); until std-term session 8 (review finding STERM-R2-10) the Rust and Go columns appended to growable containers and the C and Zig buffers were not zeroed.

Every column, Mk included, runs the same scalar scan into one buffer allocated once (sanitize.c's loop; std-term session 6, TERM-13 and TERM-14). Until session 6 the Mk column ran std's term.Sanitize, whose 16-byte vector scan and validating Text sink broke this table's contract (same loop, same data structures, no hand vectorisation); its numbers are superseded. std's term.Sanitize has no fair row yet: a SIMD-table row needs SIMD peers and a non-validating byte Writer for Mk (std-term request 6).
Checksums agree in all five columns at both sizes on the owner's machine (std-term session 1, 2026-11-13; the scalar Mk column gave 65423398 and 392884 again in session 6).
Not published: no number here is a measurement.
